 Line-ups 
 Watch & listen 2 
 Summary
 Wales beat New Zealand for the first time since 1953
 Tomos Williams , Dewi Lake and Archie Griffin cross for Wales, with New Zealand levelling at the break through Cortez Ratima , Wallace Sititi and Fehi Fineanganofo 
 Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit put Wales back in front before Peter Lakai pulls one back, but hosts hold on for historic win

 Literally broke down in tears. What a performance! Take a bow lads! Huge boost to their confidence!
 Aaron, Warringon 
 They've done what the greats of the 70s couldn't (quite) do! SO proud of you lads!
 JE, London 
 I'm so sorry boys; I really didn't think you could do it. My dad was at the 1953 game, he's 91 and watching today. So proud of the whole team.
 Huw, Bath 
 Congratulations Wales!! You deserve this match. One happy England fan here for our neighbours in Wales. To the beat the All Blacks is a major feat.
 Elizabeth, Hampshire

 Congratulations Wales
 David, Lincoln 
 No words.
 Patricia, Tenerife 
 Absolutely fabulous Wales! Congratulations from an Ireland supporter. Well deserved!

 get involved Get Involved published at 16:19 GMT 16:19 GMT 
 FT: Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 This is absolutely Herculean defending from Wales. Top drawer international rugby.
 Michael, Cheltenham 
 Given what Wales results and Welsh rugby have gone through the last few years, this will feel so much more emotional than just since 1953. One of the all time rugby performances, not just for Wales. Hats off to them.
 Ben, East Midlands

 'Everyone was writing us off' published at 16:17 GMT 16:17 GMT 
 FT: Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency Player of the match James Botham speaking on S4C: 
 "I honestly can't describe the feeling. 
 "I imagine everyone was writing us off, obviously the last win was 1953, so to get that historic win now just shows how far we've come and how much we're gelling as a team. 
 "I can't wait for the next game already."

 Wales defeat All Blacks 'against all odds' published at 16:14 GMT 16:14 GMT 
 Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 James Hook 
Former Wales fly-half on BBC Radio Wales 
 Wales, against all odds, they've come out with
a victory they thoroughly deserve.

 Post published at 16:12 GMT 16:12 GMT 
 Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 Ian Gough 
Former Wales international on BBC Radio Wales 
 Absolutely incredible. That was an effort deserving of a win against the All Blacks, and we will all remember where we were during this brilliant Test match.
 797 35 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:11 GMT 16:11 GMT 
 FT: Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 It's just been revealed that New Zealand were given a 96% chance of winning this Test at half-time.
 Wales' four percenters have produced the goods.
 'Rhythm is a dancer' is the rather odd choice for a celebration song.
 The players from both sides are still out there on this day to remember.
 Wales are now going on their lap of honour.
 There were 55,000 in this stadium - far from a sell-out - and those punters will not regret shelling out for those tickets.
 610 36 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:08 GMT 16:08 GMT 
 FT: Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 Wales gather for a team photo on the pitch, the first team to have a victory shot after stunning the All Blacks since 1953.
 Sadly it is without captain Dewi Lake, who is carrying out his post-match media duties.
 The streak is over.
 Only the players and staff saw this coming.
 774 34 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:07 GMT 16:07 GMT 
 FT: Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 Lloyd Williams 
Wales scrum-half on BBC Radio Cymru 
 People have been very negative about this team, and they have responded. 
 807 38 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:06 GMT 16:06 GMT 
 FT: Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 There is joy from those in red while the players in black cannot believe what has happened.
 They just couldn't find a way through that Red Wall in the 22.
 Plenty of supporters from New Zealand are not hanging around. They didn't want to witness history being made.
 664 35 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:05 GMT 16:05 GMT 
 FT: Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 Catatonia blasts out as Wales' players hug.
 Ex-Lions flanker Dan Lydiate is among them and he would have been so proud of that defensive effort.
 James Botham is named as man of the match.
 893 26 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 16:02 GMT 16:02 GMT 
 FT: Wales 35-28 New Zealand 
 WALES HAVE BEATEN NEW ZEALAND FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE 1953!
 After 34 straight defeats, Steve Tandy's side have upset the odds.
 A remarkable victory earned by resolute defence.
 This is quite unbelievable.
 There are tears in the stands.
 Image source, Huw Evans Picture Agency
